From the Windows box, on TP-467 (#104), three things for waves B to D; nothing claimed, no ids minted. (1) Scope gap: TP-467 scopes cc/GOAL.md out as a project record, but the failure here is a same-machine one. A background session hands off inside a Claude Code worktree, whose isolation refuses writes to the main checkout, and a gitignored cc/GOAL.md never exists in a worktree, while the banner reads the main checkout's goal (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). Seen here: the banner opened on a goal two days stale and every handoff asked the operator to copy a draft by hand. (2) Wave C, read from the pack, not driven: if hooks re-root on the worktree of the payload's cwd, a worktree session's banner finds no goal at all rather than a stale one, so the goal read needs its own answer beside the plan and flags. One shape measured in a scratch repo: a local, never-pushed ref (say refs/espalier/goal) written from a linked worktree reads back from the main checkout, and update-ref with the old value refuses a stale second writer. (3) Sister site, probable, not driven: scripts/record_snapshot.py roots at the checkout it runs from (REPO_ROOT from __file__), so a handoff from a worktree on your box would snapshot the worktree's sparse untracked set and the record tip would drop the main checkout's blueprints, reports and goal (history keeps them; the zero-file refusal does not fire). Worth a guard before wave B makes worktree sessions routine. Our stopgap, no code: this box's main-checkout cc/GOAL.md is now a pointer, and worktree handoffs carry the notes in the worktree's working summary.
